subject: Evidence pack request: model-improvement opt-out, prompt/response ownership, and export controls
messages:
From: Mara Santos <mara.santos@novamed.com>
To: Jordan Blake <jordan_blake@redwood.ai>
Date: Mon, 2 Nov 2026 09:12:00 -0800
Subject: Data use confirmation + evidence pack request

Hi Jordan,

Thanks for the product demo last week — our technical and legal teams reviewed Redwood's architecture and we have a couple of follow-ups before we can proceed with a PO. The Legal Ops team asked me to confirm the following: 

1) A clear statement that customer-provided prompts and generated responses will not be used to improve or retrain models ("no-training" or model-improvement opt-out) and whether that is available for our planned hosted deployment.
2) Confirmation of who owns the prompt/response outputs (customer IP / output ownership language) and whether Redwood would assert any derivative rights.
3) A current list of subprocessors, their hosting regions, and whether any subprocessors have access to unredacted prompt/response data.
4) Evidence of controls for cross-border data transfers (esp. US->EU) and any export-control limitations.

Attached is our standard vendor evidence request form — can you provide an evidence pack and proposed contract language we can share with our procurement/legal team? Also flag items that would require Dedicated or Private deployment vs. hosted API.

Goal: get confirmation and a DPA amendment we can send to our procurement team by end of week.

Thanks,
Mara Santos
Head of Legal Ops
Novamed Health

Attachment: vendor-evidence-request.pdf (form)

From: Jordan Blake <jordan_blake@redwood.ai>
To: Mara Santos <mara.santos@novamed.com>
Cc: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.ai>, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>
Date: Mon, 2 Nov 2026 10:05:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Data use confirmation + evidence pack request

Mara — thanks for the clear list. Looping in Karthik (privacy & legal liaison) and Marissa (account lead) so we can get you a consolidated response + artifacts. High level answers up front:

- No-model-improvement (commercial commitment): We offer a contractual "no-model-improvement" clause. For Dedicated and Private deployments we can guarantee no model improvement on customer data. For Hosted API, we offer a contractual opt-out and technical safeguards (short-term retention, access controls) but some enterprise customers prefer Dedicated/Private for absolute isolation.

- Output ownership: Redwood's standard DPA states customers retain ownership of their inputs and outputs; we do not claim derivative rights over customer prompts/responses. We can provide redline language if you want explicit IP clause text.

- Subprocessors: attaching our current subprocessor registry (subprocessor_list_2026.csv). Karthik: can you confirm whether any subprocessors have operational access to unredacted request/response data in hosted tier?

- Cross-border transfers: we have a documented transfer matrix and SCC-based transfers for EU customers. We'll include the section of the DPA that covers transfers and encryption controls.

Attachments I'm adding now: redwood-dpa-annotated.pdf (annotated DPA calling out the clauses you asked about) and subprocessor_list_2026.csv.

Next steps: Karthik will follow up with the technical/evidence notes and a short SOP summary for the no-train option. Marissa will set up a quick call with procurement if you'd like.

Best,
Jordan Blake
Enterprise Account Executive
Redwood Inference

Attachments: redwood-dpa-annotated.pdf, subprocessor_list_2026.csv

From: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.ai>
To: Mara Santos <mara.santos@novamed.com>, Jordan Blake <jordan_blake@redwood.ai>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>
Date: Tue, 3 Nov 2026 11:40:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Data use confirmation + evidence pack request

Hi Mara — quick technical notes to supplement Jordan's summary. Apologies for verbosity, but want to be precise so your legal/procurement team can map controls to the questions on the form.

1) No-model-improvement / opt-out: 
- For Dedicated and Private: contractual + technical enforcement. Data never enters our model improvement pipelines and persistent logging for training is disabled.
- For Hosted API: we provide a contractual commitment to not use customer-provided prompts/responses to improve general models when the customer opts out. Operationally this is enforced by request tagging and retention flags; however, some internal telemetry (anonymized metrics, system logs) are retained for reliability/abuse detection — we can provide a short SOP describing the exact telemetry types and retention windows.

2) Prompt/response access and ownership:
- Customers retain exclusive rights to prompts/responses. Redwood personnel access is role-based and audited. Only staff with explicit privilege (SRE or support engineers with an approved ticket) can view unredacted requests in hosted mode; access is logged and requires Just-In-Time approval for sensitive accounts.

3) Subprocessor access:
- Most subprocessors provide infra (cloud regions, object storage, monitoring). None of the named subprocessors have ongoing direct access to unredacted customer data by default. For hosted support cases, limited authorized personnel may view redacted/unredacted data under an access workflow. We can provide a redacted sample access log and the SOP for responding to support data-access requests.

4) Cross-border and export controls:
- We support EU data residency via region-specific endpoints and standard contractual clauses. Exports that would trigger export-control review (e.g., certain dual-use categories) are flagged by our compliance workflow — we'll add that matrix.

Attachments: no-train-sop-summary.pdf (two-page summary of operational controls), and a sample redacted support-access log (redacted_support_access_log.csv).

If Novamed needs "attestation" or SOC2 artifacts we can provide SOC2 Type II report under NDA and a clean-roomed extract of the subprocessor access controls.

Karthik
Head of Privacy & Compliance
Redwood Inference

Attachments: no-train-sop-summary.pdf, redacted_support_access_log.csv

From: Legal Ops <legal-ops@novamed.com>

Jordan/Karthik — thank you for the quick responses and the artifacts so far. A few clarifying asks before we route to procurement: 

- Can you provide the exact clause text you propose to add to the DPA for the no-model-improvement opt-out (we prefer to see contract language we can redline)?
- We need an explicit statement on retention windows for hosted requests and the maximum time unredacted prompts/responses could exist in logs/backups (if any).
- Please confirm whether the subprocessors listed in subprocessor_list_2026.csv are subject to RBC-equivalent controls and whether you will notify us of any changes within 30 days.
- We will need proof of SOC2 Type II (last 12 months) and a redacted sample of an access log showing a support access event for troubleshooting (with clear timestamps and approver).

If any of the deliverables require a Dedicated/Private deployment (rather than the hosted API), please flag that explicitly — our procurement is sensitive to migration cost. If you can get us the clause text and the SOC2 proof and the redacted access log by EOD Nov 5 that would be ideal.

Thanks,
Novamed Legal Ops

Attachment: internal_request_tracker.xlsx

Thanks — summary and deliverables below. We appreciate the timeline; we can meet the EOD Nov 5 ask for draft items.

Deliverables we will send by EOD Nov 5 (attached or link):
- Draft DPA amendment language ("no-model-improvement" clause) — plain-language and line-level redline ready for your counsel.
- Explicit retention table for hosted requests and telemetry (max retention for unredacted support copies: 30 days, backups/anonymized telemetry: 90 days).
- SOC2 Type II cover letter and secure link to the report (requires NDA) — we'll provide the signed NDA template if you want it today.
- Redacted support-access sample log (with timestamps and approver ids).
- Confirmation: All current subprocessors are included in subprocessor_list_2026.csv and we commit to 30-day notice for additions that affect data access.

Notes on Hosted vs Dedicated/Private: 
- Most items above are available for Hosted API. For a contractual guarantee that data absolutely never touches shared model-improvement systems, Dedicated or Private provides the cleanest enforcement model and may be preferable if Novamed requires cryptographic separation or on-prem storage. We will note which clauses are "Hosted-OK" vs "Dedicated/Private required" in the amendment.

Next steps:
